subject.declared_domain: The write path by which the frontend co-evolution CSE producer materializes its per-producer watermark: a single S3 JSON object recording the last-emitted portal HEAD, used as the default --since bound on the next run and declared as the leg-5 freshness marker. Covers _write_watermark (:143-151) and its call site at :269. It does NOT cover this file's local JSONL batch write (carded separately as W3-dljc), and it does NOT cover the branch-head marker family at warehouse/_branch_head.main.json -- a different object with a different writer set, carded as W3-uuxp.

methodology.how: At the end of a successful --emit, and only if write_marker is true, emit() calls _write_watermark(head, len(acc)) (:269). That function builds a four-field dict -- producer, last_emitted_head, emitted_at, n_emitted_last_run (:146-148) -- and PUTs it to a fixed S3 key with ContentType application/json (:149-150), then prints an OK line naming the bucket, key and the first 12 chars of the head (:151). The value written is the COMPUTE HEAD returned by ensure_git_synced (:247), not the newest commit in the emitted set -- so the watermark advances to what the run computed over, even on a run that emitted zero CSEs. ⛔ THIS PATH IS THE STATE THAT MAKES THE PRODUCER INCREMENTAL. Its object is read back by _read_watermark (:133-140) as the default delta bound at :250; without it, :251 leaves since_shas None and coevolution_cses skips its window filter at :170 entirely.

declared_opinions: ABSENT WATERMARK MEANS FULL BACKFILL (:134, :139-140). The code declares that no marker is an honest signal to backfill everything. That is a position about how to interpret missing state, and it is the position that makes this path's absence invisible -- see failure_mode.
THE MARKER IS SUPPRESSIBLE FOR DEV USE (:381, --no-marker). A declared escape hatch that lets the sibling batch be produced with no state advance at all, leaving no record that the run happened.

ONE OBJECT SERVES TWO PURPOSES (:91, comment). The same key is declared as BOTH the --since watermark AND 'the S3 object leg-5 watches (option b)' -- a freshness signal. Those are different consumers with different tolerances for staleness, joined by a decision rather than by a derivation.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: ON THE WRITE SIDE, LOUD BY OMISSION: _write_watermark (:143-151) has NO try/except. A PutObject failure -- denied, throttled, unroutable -- propagates out of emit() and crashes the run with a traceback. Because it is called at :269, AFTER the batch file is written at :262-265 and after the OK lines are printed, a failure here leaves a fully-written valid batch on disk and a run that exited non-zero. ⛔ ON THE READ SIDE, THE OPPOSITE AND IT IS THE DEFECT: _read_watermark (:133-140) wraps its get_object in a BARE `except Exception` that returns None. Absent object, denied credentials, network failure, throttling, and malformed JSON ALL return None, and None is consumed at :250 as a positive instruction to backfill everything.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ THE PRIMARY ONE: the bare except at :139 converts INSTRUMENT FAILURE INTO A VERDICT. A permissions regression on this key is indistinguishable from a genuine first run -- both silently become a full backfill. The code's own comment names two different causes and assigns them one outcome: 'absent/no-access -> honest full backfill on the first run'. It is honest about the first-run case and silently wrong about the no-access one, and no log line separates them.

The full backfill that results is not itself an error -- it re-emits every historical session, and the deterministic event_ids at :178 make the downstream re-ingest idempotent. So the degrade is invisible in the OUTPUT as well as in the logs: a backfill and a correct incremental emit differ only in volume, and volume is exactly what the sparsity design says not to read as a signal.
The marker is suppressible with --no-marker (:381), so a run can produce a real batch and advance no state at all, leaving nothing to distinguish it from a run that never happened.

The watermark advances to the COMPUTE HEAD (:269 passes ensure_git_synced's return), not to the newest commit actually emitted. A run that emits zero CSEs still advances the watermark past that window -- correct for the declared design, but it means the marker records what was LOOKED AT, not what was DELIVERED, and a consumer reading it as delivery evidence would be wrong.

The same object is declared to serve two consumers with different staleness tolerances -- the --since bound and leg-5's freshness watch (:91). A value correct for one can be misleading for the other, and no field distinguishes the two readings.

The leg-5 watcher end is UNMEASURED. If nothing watches this key, its absence has been generating no signal for the entire period it has not existed -- which is consistent with the observed estate, where nothing anywhere records that this marker is missing.
